content.text:
As climate change intensifies and reshapes our world, we need an energy revolution for a ‘just energy transition 💬️’. But what does this term truly mean beyond emission reduction? A just energy transition is more than a climate imperative; it is a moral and social responsibility that demands our attention.

This transition must holistically address climate mitigation and adaptation, ensuring that the social and gender dimensions are central to the process. The real challenge lies as much in how we decarbonize as in determining who benefits from this transformation and who bears its costs.

First chapter of this module explores the concept of a just energy transition in the context of other energy transitions. It also reviews the concept's roots, potential and main challenges. Further on in this lesson, you will have the opportunity to explore this concept as it works in practice.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: The Energy Transition In Context
lessons.description: This lesson explores how a just transition is about more than just technical solutions or policy frameworks; it is about addressing deep-rooted socio-economic disparities, fostering participatory governance, and empowering all stakeholders to engage in the transition process.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Unpacking The Concept Of A Just Energy Transition
lessons.description: This lesson outlines the just energy transition, focusing on fairness, equity, and inclusivity in sustainable energy shifts. Originating from labor rights, it addresses historical inequities through environmental, climate, and energy justice. It highlights localized solutions and global frameworks like the AJET principles to balance urgent climate action with social and economic justice.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Key Challenges In The Global South
lessons.description: This lesson delves into the specific challenges and opportunities that developing countries face in the context of the just energy transition. By examining these dynamics, we aim to shed light on strategies and initiatives that can facilitate a transition towards a more sustainable and equitable energy future for all.
